claims.statement: get_reviewer_agent copies the incoming config before mutating it so it does not clobber the caller's recursion_limit.

PrepareReviewerRunMiddleware performs deterministic non-LLM setup before the first model call: it ensures the sandbox, mints and caches a repo-scoped GitHub App installation token as a bot token, and clones-or-fetches plus force-checks-out the PR head via prepare_review_repo.

The reviewer computes a unified diff and the set of in-diff (file, line) tuples during run prep and passes both as diff_text and diff_line_set in run state so add_finding can validate at creation time rather than at GitHub-publish time.

Author-controlled inputs (PR title/body, existing review-thread comments, finding replies) are wrapped in XML data blocks whose closing tags are neutralized by _escape_for_data_block and whose logins are validated against the GitHub username grammar, so a PR body cannot break out of its wrapper or inject instructions.

The Finding TypedDict records severity, confidence, category, title, file plus start/end line and side, in_diff, description, optional suggestion, status, first_seen/last_confirmed SHAs, GitHub comment/thread/resolved-thread id lists, surface_state, human-reply bookkeeping, diff_hunk, a content fingerprint, and an interactions log.
Finding surface states only ever move forward, so normalization of a legacy record reconciles contradictions by taking the furthest-along state.

add_finding rejects any finding whose start_line..end_line range is not part of the PR diff, returning success:false with in_diff:false so the model does not re-anchor or retry; out-of-diff findings are disabled.
add_finding resolves diff context from run state first, then configurable, then a fresh fetch_pr_diff, and stores an extracted diff_hunk on the finding when diff text is available.
Each published inline comment embeds an open-swe-review-comment JSON marker so later runs can re-locate the finding's GitHub thread by finding id.

publish_review returns a structured result the model must inspect because success:true alone does not confirm a posted review: skipped_empty_re_review with review_id null means a skipped empty re-review, dry_run:true means eval-mode simulation, and unresolvable_findings lists findings that could not be posted.

The analyzer graph learns a per-repo review-style prompt for the reviewer by mining historical human PR review feedback and the reviewer's own past finding outcomes, reusing the sandbox and gh pattern with a user OAuth or App token wired into the sandbox proxy.

The analyzer's save_review_style_prompt tool persists the synthesized custom_prompt (plus summary, reviewers, and counts) to the REVIEW_STYLES store keyed by review_style_full_name and marks the record completed.

On a successful save_review_style_prompt, ensure_continual_cron idempotently registers one daily LangGraph continual-learning cron per repo, staggered by a hash of the repo name across 05:00-08:59 UTC.

ReviewStyle records are stored in the typed `review_styles` namespace and track analysis status, prompt and sampling metadata, analysis thread/run identifiers, cron identifier, error, and timestamps; reviewer prompt lookup fails soft if this store is unavailable.

Bootstrap analysis collects samples before creating a durable analyzer run and marks the style record failed if collection or run startup fails; an immediate continual run uses the same deterministic review-style thread.
A missing reviewer thread is converted to a structured do-not-retry tool result because retry cannot restore evicted, evaluation-mode, or never-created durable finding state.
The reviewer, analyzer, and review-scout are three separately registered LangGraph graph entrypoints.
The review-scout graph is invoked during reviewer preparation for a PR-head walkthrough; the reviewer waits at most 600 seconds and continues without it after failure or timeout.
ReviewScoutTarget reuses a walkthrough for its target head, joins an active run only for that same head, and starts a new run when active work is for an older head.
Scout preparation uses a replaceable App-token sandbox and merge-base working tree; after execution it stores an ordered walkthrough only when finalization yields a non-other step.

Production findings are persisted in PostgreSQL under a pull request, with one-time migration of legacy thread-metadata findings; evaluation runs instead use bounded process-local run-scoped findings.
Reconciliation matches markers before remembered IDs, records human replies as needs-reassessment interactions, and resolves an open finding only when every matched terminal thread is resolved.
publish_review requires a complete unique ranking for all candidates and limits re-review publication to findings first seen at the current head.
Analyzer skill playbooks are virtual run-input files mounted at `/skills/` via a StateBackend rather than written into the execution sandbox.

A scheduled continual analyzer run has no accumulating message history but supplies the deterministic style thread ID, continual mode, and skill files; without a thread ID the analyzer factory returns an empty agent.
